q: Does the acquired-radioresistance phenotype of HepG2-R (near-zero alpha, larger beta) survive a source-modality swap: Co-60 gamma vs LINAC 6-MV photons vs orthovoltage 250-kVp x-rays?
basis: The Huang et al. LQ fits are all on a single Co-60 geometry. The near-zero alpha of HepG2-R is unusual and could be partly an artifact of the low-LET Co-60 spectrum + specific dose-rate. Cross-modality comparisons would separate a true intrinsic-repair phenotype from a source-specific dose-response.
next_steps: Retrospective meta-analysis of published HepG2/HepG2-R clonogenic curves across sources (searchable via PubMed + CellRepo). Refit LQ to each series and test whether the alpha-suppressed shape is source-invariant. No wet lab needed. Free endpoints: PubMed + Google Scholar.

q: Can the RBE amplification ratio (RBE_HepG2-R / RBE_HepG2 ~ 1.62) be predicted from first-principles LET spectra of the thermal-neutron + B-10(n,alpha) field, independent of the wet-lab dose-survival fit?
basis: RBE amplification on a resistant line ought to follow from the microdosimetric spectrum of the alpha + Li-7 recoil products and the alpha-only-quadratic MKM/LEM prediction. The paper does not do this: it only reports experimental RBE. A theory-first prediction would provide an independent check on the wet-lab number.
next_steps: Use the published MKM (Microdosimetric Kinetic Model) or LEM-IV parameters for HepG2-family cells; feed the thermal-neutron + B-10 LET spectrum from an open MCNP/Geant4 BNCT deck (e.g., THOR reactor benchmark published in Appl. Radiat. Isot.) and compute predicted RBE10 per line. Compare vs 3.68 and 5.97. Compute is modest (single-node CPU).

q: Does BNCT retain its selective advantage on other radioresistant tumor types beyond HCC (e.g., glioblastoma stem cells, pancreatic PDAC, radioresistant melanoma)?
basis: The Huang paper establishes the effect on one lineage. Whether the mechanism (heavy-ion-like DSB clustering + G2/M arrest + apoptosis re-sensitization) generalizes across radioresistant phenotypes with different repair backgrounds (BRCA1/2 status, ATM status) is unclear.
next_steps: Systematic search of BNCT clonogenic data in DepMap-annotated cell lines cross-referenced with published radiation-resistance panels. Rank by repair-pathway status. Predict which resistance archetypes should benefit most from BNCT vs conventional radiotherapy. Free endpoints: DepMap portal + CellosaurusRRIDs + PubMed.

q: How sensitive is the RBE result to intra-tumoral B-10 uptake heterogeneity, and could an in-silico tumor-heterogeneity model change the conclusion?
basis: The paper reports a mean ~58-59 ppm B-10 plateau but does not present per-cell or per-region uptake distributions. Because the B-10(n,alpha) dose scales linearly with local B-10 concentration and the alpha range is ~10 microns, uptake heterogeneity translates directly into dose heterogeneity and could bias the population-averaged RBE substantially.
next_steps: Build a simple stochastic uptake model: draw per-cell B-10 concentrations from a lognormal with mean 58 ppm and CV in [0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 1.0]; compute predicted SF distribution; compare mean SF vs paper-reported SF. This is a Python notebook, no new experiments. Publicly available BPA/BSH uptake CV data can seed the priors.

q: Can an ML-driven boron-carrier / dose-schedule optimizer close the gap between mean-field BNCT dose and what the tumor actually receives?
basis: Current BNCT clinical dosimetry uses a single ppm-B-10 measurement to compute a single boron dose. The Huang paper implicitly assumes uniform uptake. Modern boron carriers (dodecaborate lipid conjugates, boronated albumin) plus surrogate uptake imaging (F-18-BPA PET) could enable per-voxel dose optimization, but this has not been formally optimized end-to-end.
next_steps: Prototype a Bayesian-optimization or surrogate-model pipeline: input F-18-BPA PET voxel B-10 distribution + thermal-neutron fluence map; output per-fraction dose optimized to minimize normal-liver dose subject to a tumor-D95 constraint. Publicly-available BPA-PET phantoms exist in the QIN/QIBA archives. No wet lab; simulation only.
